interface.title: Predicting Antibiotic Resistance Across Bacterial Mechanisms Using Machine Learning (Streamlit app: Home / Report / Virtual Lab)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploring and interpreting model predictions; reading how the model was validated
interface.what_it_is_for: Pick a bacterium and an antibiotic, then compare a fixed-formula resistance score (V1) with a gradient-boosting prediction (V2) and the ATLAS surveillance rate when there is one. A donut chart splits the V1 formula's weighted sum by resistance mechanism, and the Report shows which features the V2 model relies on.

data.note: The app ships its own tables. Table A records which mechanisms each of 12 bacteria has, and Table B gives each of 22 antibiotics' vulnerability weight per mechanism, for 264 bacterium–antibiotic pairs. ATLAS observed rates cover 84 of those pairs. Nothing was uploaded. The Virtual Lab's default pair is Acinetobacter baumannii + Amikacin. The Table A, Table B and 'Super Table (Cross Join)' shown on the Report page are toy A/B/C illustrations, not the real data.

features.name: Contribution donut chart with legend toggling
features.general: Show, as a donut chart, how a fixed weighted formula's score splits across factors for one item; the shares are of the formula's weighted sum, not of any predicted value. Hovering gives the name and percentage, and clicking legend entries hides factors so the remaining shares re-normalise.
features.specific: An ECharts donut, 'Antibiotic Resistance Percentage by Mechanism', redrawn for each pair. Each slice is a mechanism's weight divided by the pair's total vulnerability (the V1 formula's weighted sum); it does not break down V2 or the ATLAS rate. It shows only the mechanisms that bacterium has, and the legend changes too (e.g. intrinsic_beta_lactamase, non_fermenter). Hovering shows the mechanism name in large text in the centre plus a % tooltip. Clicking a legend name hides or restores that slice, and the % values recalculate (16.67% → 20%). The hidden state resets when the pair changes.
steps: Choose a pair so the donut redraws for it
Hover a slice to read the mechanism name and its % share of the V1 weighted sum
Click a legend name to hide that mechanism; the other shares re-normalise
Click more legend names to hide several, or click again to restore
Pick another pair; the legend resets to show every mechanism
serves_tasks: See how the rule-based score's weight splits across factors for one item

I could not see the full list of 84 ATLAS-covered pairs anywhere in the interface. Coverage can only be found one pair at a time, through the no-ATLAS message.
The real Table A and Table B (the mechanism matrix and vulnerability weights) are not shown. The Report's tables are placeholder A/B/C examples.

The donut shows each mechanism's share of the V1 formula's weighted sum. It is not scaled by the V1 or V2 resistance value, so it cannot show how much any one mechanism adds to the predicted or observed rate.
Figure 3 is titled 'LOOCV', but its caption says the points are in-sample predictions from the model trained on all 84 pairs. I noted the contradiction but could not resolve it from the interface.
Whether leaving the Virtual Lab page resets both dropdowns to the default pair was not tested.
Screening was limited to two drugs per bacterium and two bacteria per drug; no full ranking across all 22 antibiotics or 12 bacteria was made.
Bacteria with identical mechanism profiles (e.g. E. coli vs Salmonella) were never compared on the same antibiotic.
I did not open the Streamlit main menu (⋮) or Deploy. They are framework controls, not part of the science tool.
